name: Attiéké
subtitle: Attiéké is a dish made from steamed cassava: the tubers are ground and mixed with fermented cassava to make a semolina, which is then steamed.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A dish made from steamed cassava tubers.

facts.label: How it is made
facts.value: The cassava is ground and mixed with fermented cassava to make a semolina, which is then steamed.

facts.label: Who makes it
facts.value: Traditionally produced by women for household consumption.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Produced by the lagoon peoples of Côte d’Ivoire.

facts.label: Distribution
facts.value: After cooling it is packaged and distributed in baskets lined with cassava leaves.

facts.label: Ceremonies
facts.value: A staple food at inaugurations, weddings, baptisms and funeral ceremonies.

facts.label: Place in the diet
facts.value: Accounts for about 5% of food expenses and 20.5% of calories in the diet of many Ivorian populations.

facts.label: UNESCO inscription
facts.value: Inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity at the 19th session of the Committee (Asunción, 2024).

facts.label: Eaten with
facts.value: A slightly sour cassava semolina that accompanies fish and meat in sauce.

facts.label: When it is eaten
facts.value: Eaten every day and at ceremonies such as weddings, baptisms and funerals (Côte d’Ivoire's permanent delegate to UNESCO).

facts.label: Geographical indication
facts.value: In 2023 the African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) registered “attiéké des lagunes” as a protected geographical indication.

parts.text: Attiéké is a dish made from steamed cassava: the tubers are ground and mixed with fermented cassava to make a semolina, which is then steamed. It is associated with the lagoon peoples of Côte d’Ivoire and is traditionally produced by women. In 2024 UNESCO inscribed the skills related to its production on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
It is eaten every day and at ceremonies such as weddings, baptisms and funerals, usually with fish or meat in sauce.
